cover letter

01. Which statement below best describes the highest level of education you have completed? Options: Some High School | High school graduate, diploma or the equivalent (GED) | Some college (less than 60 units) | Associate degree or at least 60 semester units | Bachelor's degree | Master's degree | Professional degree | Doctorate degree

02. How many years of professional food storage or warehouse operations experience do you have? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year of experience | 1 year but less than 2 years of experience | 2 years but less than 3 years experience | 3 years but less than 4 years experience | 4 years experience or more

03. Which of the following areas of warehouse operations do you have professional work experience in? (Select all that apply.) Options: Receiving, inspecting, and processing incoming shipments. | Inventory control, stock replenishment, and cycle counting. | Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) or electronic inventory tracking. | Order picking, packing, staging, and distribution. | Shipping, logistics, and delivery coordination. | Food warehousing, including dry, refrigerated, and frozen storage. | Warehouse safety, sanitation, and regulatory compliance. | None of the above.

04. Which of the following best describes the size and scale of the warehouse operations you have managed or coordinated? (Select all that apply.) Options: Less than 100,000 sq. ft. | 100,000–249,999 sq. ft. | 250,000–499,999 sq. ft. | 500,000 sq. ft. or more | I do not have warehouse operations experience.

05. Based on your food storage or warehouse operations experience, please provide details for your MOST RELEVANT positions. For each position, include: (a) Job Title: (b) Organization/Agency Name: (c) Key Relevant Duties: (d) Employment Period: (From MM/YYYY to MM/YYYY) If you have no relevant experience in this area, enter "N/A."

06. How many years of experience do you possess in a Supervisory capacity, specifically overseeing warehousing staff? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year | 1 year but less than 2 years | 2 years but less than 3 years | 3 years but less than 4 years | 4 years or more

Oversees daily operations, including the planning, organizing, receiving, storing, distributing, transporting and delivering of all department products while ensuring proper inventory management and food safety compliance.
Establishes food storage keeping standards and procedures and ensures compliance with Food Service Department procedures, consults with immediate supervisor as necessary.
Supervises and participates in the inspection of food shipments received for conformity to purchase order specifications.
Process and monitor incoming shipments, rejecting and documenting spoiled or damaged food items to ensure only quality foods are received and accepted.

Maintains accurate inventory records, reviewing and approving pick tickets, monitoring equipment repairs and ensuring adherence to state and federal health codes regulations within the warehouse coolers and freezers.
Plans and participates in the salvage and disposal activities of the district.
Supervises and participates in periodic or special inventory and stock control programs for equipment and supplies.

Maintains the warehouse, freezers, coolers, and operating equipment throughout the district in a clean, orderly, safe, and secure condition, and establishes a system of preventative maintenance for the equipment.
Operates forklifts, pallet jacks, and assigned vehicles.
Takes necessary action to prepare materials for shipment.
Maintains a safety program.
Supervises, trains, and assists in evaluation of assigned staff.
Manages site kitchen needs, makes equipment recommendations to enhance food quality and coordinates the installation, maintenance and repair of department equipment.
Performs related duties as assigned.
Food warehousing and inventory control methods and procedures.
Methods of receiving, inspecting, and issuing food item materials utilized in a Food Services Department.
Principles of storing and shipping perishable and non-perishable foods, including stock rotation and temperature control
Commercial food preparation equipment.
Inventory management systems (WMS, ERP) and software used in Nutrition Services
Principles and practices of staff supervision, training, and performance management
Plan, o rganize and coordinate activities of Nutrition Services warehouse operations.
Maintain accurate and current records of food inventory transactions.
Lift, move, sort, and store food related objects.
Operate a forklift, and other warehouse equipment.
Supervise, assign, review, and evaluate the performance of assigned staff.
Prioritize multiple tasks simultaneously.
Remain abreast of procurement trends related to responsibilities.
Work cooperatively with others.
Operate inventory management systems and Nutrition Services software.
Understand and follow HACCP, Cal/OSHA safety, County Health Department and other federal and state rules and regulations.
Model communications and interactions that respect and include all individuals and their languages, abilities, religions, and cultures.
